Rashi on Shabbat 40a:1:1.hebrew: הדר ביה רבי עקיבא - כדאמרינן בפירקין דלעיל (שבת דף כט:). לשון מכריע — מכביד, מטה כף מאזנים ומכריע את שכנגדו. כגון הכא: בחמין אסור — השתא הוה ליה ר' שמעון דמתיר בחמין יחיד במקום שנים, נמצא ר' יהודה מכביד את כף המשקולת, שהרי ר' יהודה עם רבי מאיר שוים לאיסור; ובצונן מותר — הוי ליה ר' מאיר בצונן יחיד במקום שנים, נמצא ר' יהודה מכביד את כף המשקולת:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:1:1.english: Rabbi Akiva retracted - As we said in the chapter above (Shabbat 29b). The expression makhria [compromiser] denotes weighing down: tipping a scale-pan and outweighing the one opposite it. For example, here: [When Rabbi Yehuda ruled,] “With hot water [it is] forbidden” — now Rabbi Shimon, who permits with hot water, is a single individual against two, so Rabbi Yehuda is found to be weighing down the scale-pan, for Rabbi Yehuda together with Rabbi Meir are in agreement for prohibition; and [when he ruled,] “and with cold water [it is] permitted” — Rabbi Meir regarding cold water is a single individual against two, so Rabbi Yehuda is found to be weighing down the scale-pan.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:1:2.hebrew: ה"מ - דא"ר יוחנן, הלכה כדברי המכריע — במכריע במשנה, כי ההיא דמטלניות:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:1:2.english: These words - That which Rabbi Yoḥanan said, “The halakha is in accordance with the statement of the compromiser,” [was said only] regarding one who compromises in a Mishna, like that [case] of strips of cloth.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:2:1.hebrew: כעין פניו - כלומר, כל אבר בפני עצמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:2:1.english: Similar to his face - That is to say, each limb by itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:4:1.hebrew: רוחץ בהן כל גופו - ביחד, אלא שמשייר אבר אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:4:1.english: One may wash his entire body with them - all at once, except that he leaves out one limb.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:4:2.hebrew: איתיביה כל הני - וליכא לשנויי כעין פניו ידיו ורגליו, דהא כל גופו יחד קאמר, חוץ מאבר אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:4:2.english: They raised all of these [refutations] against him - And it is not possible to answer [that he meant] in the manner of his face, his hands, and his feet, for he said [that one may wash] his entire body all at once, except for one limb.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:5:1.hebrew: א"ל רב יוסף לאביי - משום דגדל אביי בבית רבה בר נחמני, שהיה ראש קודם לרב יוסף ומת, היה שואלו רב יוסף איך היה רואהו נוהג:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:5:1.english: Rav Yosef said to Abaye - Because Abaye grew up in the house of Rabba bar Nachmani, who was the head [of the yeshiva] before Rav Yosef and had died, Rav Yosef asked him how he had seen him conduct himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:5:2.hebrew: מי עביד כשמעתי' דרב - בהא מילתא דרחיצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:5:2.english: Does [he] act in accordance with Rav's teaching - In this matter of bathing.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:5:3.english: What is his dilemma - The discourse of the Talmud raises an objection against him [Rav Yosef].

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:5:4.hebrew: לא שמיע ליה - לרבה הא תיובתא. משום הכי מספקא ליה לרב יוסף ברבה, דדילמא עביד כרב:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:5:4.english: He did not hear - Rabba [had not heard] this refutation. That is why Rav Yosef was in doubt regarding Rabba, that perhaps he acts in accordance with Rav.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:6:1.english: And if he did not hear it - Why was Rav Yosef in doubt?

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:6:2.english: Behold, he certainly acted [so] - Rabba [acted] in all matters in accordance with Rav.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:6:3.hebrew: כחומרי דרב הוה עביד - בר מהני תלת חומרי, אבל כקולי דרב איכא דלא עביד. והא קולא היא, ודילמא לא עביד:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:6:3.english: He would act in accordance with the stringencies of Rav - Except for these three stringencies. But in accordance with the leniencies of Rav, there are [some] that he did not follow; and this is a leniency, and perhaps he did not follow [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:7:1.english: Whose openings were sealed - So that its heat would not escape.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:7:2.hebrew: רוחץ בו מיד - ואין צריך להמתין בכדי שיעשה. ל"א: שפקקו נקביו — אותן נקבים שמרחץ מתחמם על ידיהן, שאור ניסקת מבחוץ מתחתיו (לוי"ה). ועיקר רוחץ בו מיד — שהרי לא נתחמם בשבת; אבל בשבת לא, שהרי גזרו על הרחיצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:7:2.english: One may bathe in it immediately - And one does not need to wait the amount of time it takes to prepare [it]. Another explanation: “Whose openings were sealed” — those openings through which the bathhouse is heated, as fire is stoked from outside beneath it (la voie [the heating flues]). And the main [point of stating] “one may bathe in it immediately” [is] that it was not heated on Shabbat; but on Shabbat [one may] not, for [the Sages] decreed against bathing.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:7:3.hebrew: ומשתטף בבית החיצון - שלפני המרחץ, ולא בתוך המרחץ — שלא יאמרו רוחץ הוא, כדאמרן דאסרו את הרחיצה אבל הזיעה התירו. והיאך היא זיעה? עומד או יושב בבית המרחץ, ואינו נותן מים עליו, והוא מתחמם ומזיע:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:7:3.english: And rinses in the outer room - [Which is] in front of the bathhouse, and not inside the bathhouse — lest [people] say he is bathing, as we said, that they forbade bathing, but permitted sweating. And how is [this] sweating [done]? He stands or sits in the bathhouse and does not pour water upon himself, and he becomes heated and sweats.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:8:1.english: Covered with boards - And they did not need to be concerned lest [the water] was heated on Shabbat from the heat of the bathhouse.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:8:4.hebrew: מטייל בהן - מהלך בתוכן לפי דרכו, ולא להזיע:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:8:4.english: One may stroll through them - Walking through them in his usual manner, and not [in order] to sweat.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:8:5.hebrew: ואינו חושש - שמא יאמרו מזיע הוא, ואע"ג דאסרו את הזיעה:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:8:5.english: And he need not be concerned - Lest [people] say that he is sweating, even though they prohibited sweating.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:9:1.english: What are "transgressors" - That which [the Baraita] says above, that they prohibited sweating on their account.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:9:2.english: They prohibited hot water to them - Completely.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:9:3.hebrew: ועדיין היו רוחצין בחמין - שהוחמו מבע"י:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:9:3.english: And they would still bathe in hot water - That had been heated while it was still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:9:4.hebrew: שאין הדבר עומד - שלא היו ציבור יכולין לקבל, מתוך שאסרו להם את הכל:
Rashi on Shabbat 40a:9:4.english: That the matter was not upheld - For the public was unable to accept [it], since they had prohibited everything to them.

Rashi on Shabbat 40a:9:5.english: Remained in place - As a prohibition.

Tosafot on Shabbat 40a:1:1.hebrew: דילמא ה"מ במתני' אבל בברייתא לא - אע"ג דלא קאמר במשנתינו, הכא משמע דאין הלכה כמותו, משום דסתם מתני' דלא כוותיה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 40a:1:1.english: "Perhaps this applies in a Mishnah, but in a baraita, no" - Even though he did not say "in our Mishnah," here it implies that the halakha is not in accordance with his opinion, because an anonymous Mishnah is not in accordance with him.

Tosafot on Shabbat 40a:7:1.hebrew: למוצאי שבת רוחץ מיד - דוקא לרחוץ, אבל להזיע נכנס אפי' בשבת ומזיע, כמו בי"ט, כדאמר בסמוך: דאפי' בשבת הוי זיעה שריא עד הגזירה, ולאחר גזירה אפילו בי"ט אסרו, דאיום טוב קתני: "משרבו עוברי עבירה התחילו לאסור". והוה מצי לערובינהו וליתנינהו: "מרחץ שפקקו נקביו מערב שבת או מערב יום טוב — למחר נכנס ומזיע, ולמוצאי שבת ויום טוב רוחץ מיד". אלא אי עריב ותני להו, הוה אמינא: דדוקא בשבת אסרו הזיעה ולא ביום טוב, דעובדא דמייתי בשבת הוה; להכי מפליג להו. השתא, "משרבו עוברי עבירה" קאי איום טוב, אבל לא אשבת, דזיעה לא הוזכרה גבי שבת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 40a:7:1.english: At the conclusion of Shabbat one may bathe immediately - [This applies] specifically to bathing, but to sweat, one may enter even on Shabbat and sweat, just as on a Festival, as [the Gemara] states nearby that even on Shabbat sweating was permitted until the decree. And after the decree, they prohibited it even on a Festival, as it is taught regarding a Festival: "When transgressors multiplied, they began to prohibit [it]." And [the Tanna] could have combined them and taught them [together]: "A bathhouse whose openings were sealed on Shabbat eve or on the eve of a Festival — on the morrow one may enter and sweat, and at the conclusion of Shabbat and a Festival one may bathe immediately." Rather, had he combined and taught them [together], I would have said that specifically on Shabbat did they prohibit sweating, and not on a Festival, because the incident that [the Gemara] cites occurred on Shabbat; therefore, he separated them. Now [that he separated them], "when transgressors multiplied" applies to a Festival, but not to Shabbat, since sweating was not mentioned regarding Shabbat.

Tosafot on Shabbat 40a:8:1.hebrew: אלא שחמין שלו מחופין בנסרים - פי' בקונטרס, שלא היו צריכין לחוש שהוחמו בשבת מחום המרחץ. משמע שסובר שנשתטפו בחמין שהוחמו מע"ש — ולעיל אסר רבי יהודה גופיה! ושמא יחלק בין שבת ליום טוב. ומיהו בתוספתא גרסינן: "ונשתטפו בצונן, אלא שחמין שלו מחופים, ולא יסברו העולם שרחצו בחמין":
Tosafot on Shabbat 40a:8:1.english: "However, its hot water was covered with boards" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that they did not need to be concerned that [the water] had been heated on Shabbat from the heat of the bathhouse. This implies that he holds that they rinsed with hot water that had been heated on Shabbat eve; yet above, Rabbi Yehuda himself prohibited [this]! And perhaps [Rabbi Yehuda] would distinguish between Shabbat and Yom Tov. However, in the Tosefta our reading is: "And they rinsed with cold water; but its hot water was covered, so that people would not assume that they had bathed in hot water."
